We're coming up on Brightline's renewal window for our Redwood account — target renewal execution is July 31, 2026. Procurement and finance have asked for the most recent SOC 2 Type II report plus confirmation of audit coverage so they can close their internal PO by July 15.

Two quick asks:
- Can you share the latest Type II report and any existing or acceptable bridge/attestation language that would cover a renewal through Aug 31, 2026?
- What are the exact report period dates for your last Type II so we can confirm there isn't a coverage gap for our internal auditors?

We will likely need a short attestation (one page) that references controls unchanged since the end of the last reporting period. If possible, can you send a draft by EOD Tuesday (6/22)? Procurement will be looping in John Carter on finance questions.

Thanks —

Elena —

Thanks for the heads up and the clear timeline. Short answers up front: yes, we can provide the Type II report and a bridge letter; and I can get a draft attestation to you by EOD 6/22. Details below so your auditors can map dates to the renewal window.

1) Latest SOC 2 Type II report
- Report file: SOC2_Report_2024_TypeII.pdf (attached)
- Reporting period covered: 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-31
- Report issued: 2025-02-20 (independent auditor)

2) Audit cadence & expected next Type II
- Our next annual Type II audit covers 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31; auditor fieldwork completed early 2026 and report availability is expected by late February 2026. (If you have a specific requirement to see the 2025 report, let me know and I will flag it.)

3) Bridge / temporary attestation options to cover renewal through Aug 31, 2026
- Option A (short bridge letter): We can provide a signed bridge attestation confirming that there were no material changes to the described control environment since 2025-12-31 and that controls remain effective through 2026-06-30. Attached draft: Bridge_Letter_2025-06-30.pdf
- Option B (expanded wording): If your auditors need explicit language about specific control families (change mgmt, access, incident response), we can include callouts — will need legal review and that adds 48–72 hours.

4) Next steps / requests from Brightline
- Please confirm which option (A or B) your procurement/audit team prefers.
- Confirm the contract effective date you plan to show on the PO/renewal (we can align the attestation dates to that).
- If you require DocuSign or specific signatory name formatting, include that detail.

I'll loop in Laura from Legal and Grace from Customer Success so procurement has a direct line for contract/renewal questions and any service-impact clarifications.

Best,
Rohan Mehta
Sr. Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick reply and the attachments. Procurement prefers Option A (short bridge) for now provided the language explicitly states:
- that Redwood's control environment described in the 2024 report has not materially changed, and
- that controls remained in place through at least 2026-06-30, and
- that the bridge letter is intended to provide interim assurance until the 2025 Type II is issued.

Finance (copied: John) also asked whether the bridge letter can reference our PO/contract ID once issued. We'll add that during signature if possible.

3) Add a one-line sentence confirming there have been no change-of-control events since 2024-12-31.

If you can get that to us by EOD 6/23 we should be able to keep our internal approval timeline.

Thanks,
Elena
